runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets showed mixed performance overnight, with Japan's Nikkei 225 slipping 0.3% to close at 66,016 as investors awaited key signals from the Jackson Hole Economic Symposium set to begin this weekend. The yen held steady near recent levels as the Bank of Japan maintained its cautious stance on further rate hikes, while Chinese tech stocks continued their recovery amid regulatory easing signals from Beijing.

European markets opened broadly higher, with Germany's DAX gaining 0.59% to 26,136.56 and the FTSE 100 rising 0.64% to 10,816.56. Energy stocks led gains across the continent as Brent crude firmed above $85, while financials benefited from yield curve stabilization. The Stoxx 600 hit a fresh multi-week high as investor sentiment improved ahead of the Jackson Hole policy clarity expected from Fed Chair Powell.

US equity futures are pointing to a cautious open on Sunday August 23 as markets digest the upcoming Jackson Hole symposium where Powell is expected to speak Friday. Friday's session saw solid gains — S&P 500 +0.4%, Nasdaq +0.3%, Dow +518 pts — capping a four-week winning streak. However, the second estimate of Q2 GDP printing at a -0.9% annualized contraction and initial jobless claims ticking up to 255,000 add macro uncertainty. Volatility remains contained with VIX near 15.8, but rate-sensitive sectors face headline risk from Powell's Friday speech.

ideas.catalyst: NVIDIA reports earnings on August 26 after market close with consensus expecting record data center revenue above $35B.
ideas.thesis: NVDA remains the dominant picks-and-shovels play on the global AI infrastructure buildout, with hyperscaler capex still accelerating in H2 2026. Blackwell GPU demand continues to far outpace supply, and management tone on forward guidance has historically sent the stock 8-15% on strong beats.
ideas.key_risk: Any revenue miss or soft guidance on Blackwell supply chain could trigger a sharp post-earnings selloff.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added BAC to its August Conviction Buy List following strong Q2 results and improving NII outlook.
ideas.thesis: Bank of America's Q2 earnings demonstrated NII resilience as rate cuts begin, with consumer deposits stabilizing and credit quality holding. The Goldman conviction add brings institutional sponsorship at a time when financials are cheap on a P/B basis relative to the last two cycles.
ideas.key_risk: A faster-than-expected Fed rate cutting cycle could compress NIM and weigh on forward NII estimates.

ideas.theme: Semiconductor Equipment / GS European Conviction Add
ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added ASML to its European Conviction List in August 2026, citing semiconductor capex recovery and EUV demand inflection.
ideas.thesis: ASML holds a monopoly on extreme ultraviolet lithography equipment essential for sub-3nm chip production, and the semiconductor capex recovery cycle is gaining momentum with Intel, TSMC, and Samsung all ramping advanced node capacity. The GS conviction add reflects a view that order book inflection is near.
ideas.key_risk: Further US export restrictions to China could meaningfully reduce ASML's serviceable addressable market.

ideas.catalyst: FDA approved BMY's Zenbexus (iberdomide) for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma on August 19, expanding the company's oncology franchise.
ideas.thesis: Iberdomide addresses a large and underserved multiple myeloma patient population and is positioned as a next-generation cereblon modulator with superior efficacy to lenalidomide. The approval comes at a critical time when BMY faces Revlimid patent cliff pressure, providing meaningful revenue offset into 2027-2028.
ideas.key_risk: Competitive pressure from J&J's teclistamab and other bispecific antibody approvals could limit Zenbexus peak sales.

ideas.catalyst: FDA approved Regeneron's Pasatru to reduce new bone lesions in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) on August 19.
ideas.thesis: FOP is an ultra-rare, severely debilitating disease with no prior disease-modifying therapy, making Pasatru a first-in-class treatment with significant pricing power and limited competition. The orphan drug designation supports high ASP and long exclusivity runway, while REGN's pipeline depth in rare diseases continues to attract premium multiples.
ideas.key_risk: Ultra-rare disease market size limits commercial revenue ceiling; reimbursement negotiations with payers could delay uptake.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added AON to the August Conviction List, projecting 9%+ FCF beat vs Visible Alpha consensus for 2026-2027 driven by NFP acquisition synergies.
ideas.thesis: AON's integration of the NFP acquisition is delivering ahead-of-schedule synergies in commercial middle-market insurance brokerage, and the eventual capital markets recovery is an unpriced option. The stock trades at a reasonable premium to peers given consistent organic revenue growth and FCF compounding.
ideas.key_risk: A hard reinsurance market reversal or slower-than-expected NFP integration would pressure near-term earnings and multiple.

sources.label: Goldman Sachs Conviction List - Yahoo Finance

ideas.catalyst: Piper Sandler downgraded WEAV from Overweight to Neutral and cut price target from $8 to $7.40 on August 23.
ideas.thesis: The downgrade reflects slowing SMB dental and optometry practice software demand as macroeconomic pressure on small business tech budgets intensifies. The PT cut leaves limited upside from current levels and is likely to trigger consensus estimate revisions lower across the sell-side.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise earnings beat or strategic acquisition could create a short squeeze in this thinly-covered small-cap name.

ideas.catalyst: William Blair initiated coverage of ELVN with Outperform, citing strong ELVN-001 Phase 1 CML trial data and an $8.8B total market opportunity.
ideas.thesis: ELVN-001 is emerging as a potential best-in-class BCR-ABL inhibitor for CML patients resistant to approved TKIs, a space where clinical unmet need remains high. A William Blair Outperform initiation on a small-cap biotech typically attracts growth-oriented institutional investors and provides near-term price support.
ideas.key_risk: Early-stage clinical data is inherently uncertain; any Phase 2 setback would likely result in a substantial drawdown.

ideas.catalyst: Jackson Hole Economic Symposium begins August 23, with Fed Chair Powell expected to speak Friday amid conflicting signals of GDP contraction vs. sticky services inflation.
ideas.thesis: If Powell signals a slower-than-priced rate cutting path at Jackson Hole — citing the GDP contraction as technical rather than demand-driven — long-duration bonds face a selloff as rate cut expectations are repriced. The 10-year yield at ~4.35% has room to spike toward 4.55-4.65% if the Fed sounds more patient than the market expects.
ideas.key_risk: A dovish surprise from Powell would cause TLT to rally sharply, creating significant losses in the short position.

ideas.theme: Safe Haven / GDP Contraction / Macro Hedge
ideas.catalyst: Q2 GDP second estimate confirms -0.9% annualized contraction, raising stagflationary concerns ahead of Jackson Hole.
ideas.thesis: Gold is historically strong in stagflationary environments where growth disappoints but inflation remains elevated, limiting the Fed's ability to cut aggressively. With geopolitical uncertainty persisting and real yields potentially set to fall if growth continues to weaken, GLD offers a portfolio hedge and momentum continuation of its multi-month trend higher.
ideas.key_risk: A hawkish Jackson Hole outcome that drives real yields sharply higher would be the primary headwind for gold in the near term.

deals.headline: FDA Approves Bristol Myers Squibb's Zenbexus (Iberdomide) for Multiple Myeloma
deals.description: The FDA granted approval to BMY's Zenbexus (iberdomide), a next-generation cereblon modulator, for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma on August 19. The approval provides a meaningful growth catalyst as BMY navigates the Revlimid patent cliff, with iberdomide positioned to capture share in a multi-billion dollar market.
deals.impact: Positive for BMY revenue and pipeline credibility; mildly negative for competitors in the myeloma space

deals.headline: Regeneron Wins FDA Approval for Pasatru in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva
deals.description: Regeneron's Pasatru received FDA approval as the first disease-modifying treatment for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), an ultra-rare genetic disorder causing progressive bone formation in soft tissue. The orphan drug designation supports premium pricing and multi-year exclusivity, adding a meaningful new revenue stream to REGN's diversified portfolio.
deals.impact: Bullish for REGN; reinforces rare disease franchise alongside Dupixent and Eylea

deals.headline: Steel Knight Capital Partners Acquires TradeRunner
deals.description: Private equity firm Steel Knight Capital Partners announced the acquisition of TradeRunner, a B2B trading technology platform, on August 21 in an undisclosed deal. The transaction reflects continued PE appetite for fintech infrastructure assets with recurring SaaS revenue models despite tighter financing conditions.
deals.impact: Positive for fintech M&A sentiment; potential read-through for comparable public fintech platforms

deals.headline: NVIDIA Backs Cloverleaf Infrastructure in Strategic AI Data Center Investment
deals.description: NVIDIA made a strategic investment in Cloverleaf Infrastructure, a data center developer focused on AI-optimized compute facilities, announced August 21. The deal underscores NVIDIA's strategy to secure preferred deployment environments for its GPU hardware and aligns with the broader hyperscaler data center buildout thesis.
deals.impact: Positive for NVDA ecosystem; bullish read-through for data center REITs and power infrastructure plays

deals.headline: Anthropic Adopts Supervoting Structure Ahead of Expected IPO; Pre-IPO Credit Facility to Exceed $10B
deals.description: Anthropic, the AI safety company behind Claude, is implementing a founder supervoting share structure in preparation for its anticipated IPO, alongside a pre-IPO credit facility expected to exceed $10 billion. The move signals that an Anthropic public offering could occur within the next 12-18 months, representing one of the most anticipated tech IPOs since OpenAI's.
deals.impact: Bullish for listed AI infrastructure and software peers (GOOG, AMZN, MSFT as Anthropic investors); broad positive sentiment for AI sector

runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mixed on Friday with Japan's Nikkei 225 slipping 0.30% to 66,016 as investors awaited the upcoming Jackson Hole symposium starting Thursday. Yen strength and profit-taking in export-heavy names weighed on the index, though tech and semiconductor names held relatively firm. Chinese markets were subdued following Alibaba's announced sale of its videogame business for at least $1.5 billion, signaling continued asset rationalization at the internet giant.

European markets were broadly flat to slightly lower, with the DAX edging down 0.12% amid cautious positioning ahead of PCE data due Wednesday. The FTSE 100 was the relative outperformer, adding 0.14%, supported by commodity exposure and a mildly weaker pound. German manufacturing data continued to show marginal improvement though remains in contraction, with the broader eurozone composite PMI holding just above the 50-point expansion threshold.

US equity futures are pointing to a flat-to-slightly-higher open on what is nominally a weekend session (markets closed Saturday). The prior Friday close saw the S&P 500 gain 0.43% to 7,674 and the Nasdaq Composite rise 0.43% to 26,180, though both major indices logged back-to-back weekly losses for the first time since late July. Treasury yields stabilized near multi-month highs, with the 10-year around 4.82%, and oil was little changed near $78.45/bbl. The macro setup for the coming week is dominated by Wednesday's PCE print and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Friday speech at Jackson Hole — the first major policy signal from the new Fed chair.

ideas.catalyst: Loar Holdings remains on Goldman Sachs's Conviction Buy list following strong Q2 2026 earnings with accelerating aftermarket demand.
ideas.thesis: Loar is a niche aerospace components supplier with pricing power and long-cycle revenue streams tied to commercial aviation recovery. Goldman's conviction buy designation post-earnings signals confidence in estimate revisions higher through year-end.
ideas.key_risk: Macro slowdown or Boeing/Airbus production cuts could impair near-term demand for aircraft components.

ideas.theme: AI Infrastructure / Morgan Stanley Top Pick
ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley lists NVDA among its top stock picks for 2026; BMO Capital also made bullish calls on major chip stocks Friday.
ideas.thesis: NVIDIA's data center and AI accelerator demand continues to exceed supply, with Blackwell-architecture GPUs commanding premium pricing. The AI capex supercycle remains intact as hyperscalers ramp spending into year-end.
ideas.key_risk: Export control escalation targeting H100/Blackwell chips to China or a sudden pullback in hyperscaler AI capex could compress near-term revenue.

ideas.catalyst: FDA advisory panel voted 9-3 against the strength of evidence for deramiocel's heart benefits; August 22 is the official PDUFA target date.
ideas.thesis: With the AdCom voting heavily against, an FDA rejection on the PDUFA date is the high-probability outcome, typically resulting in a 50-80% stock decline for small-cap biotechs. Activist Kaos Capital has already begun a board campaign demanding strategic alternatives, suggesting insiders expect a setback.
ideas.key_risk: FDA could overrule the AdCom recommendation and grant accelerated approval based on unmet medical need in Duchenne cardiomyopathy; any positive surprise would trigger a violent short squeeze.

ideas.catalyst: Rothschild & Co Redburn upgraded Equifax to Buy from Neutral with a price target raised to $235 from $214 on August 21.
ideas.thesis: Equifax's mortgage inquiry volumes are recovering as rate expectations shift dovish into Jackson Hole, directly benefiting its Workforce Solutions and USIS segments. The $235 target implies roughly 12-15% upside from recent levels.
ideas.key_risk: If Jackson Hole disappoints on rate-cut signals, mortgage volumes could stall again, compressing near-term earnings estimates.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs issued a Buy on Morgan Stanley, citing underpriced M&A and capital markets activity in its pipeline; Goldman predicts an M&A boom accelerating through year-end.
ideas.thesis: Morgan Stanley's investment banking and debt/ECM revenue is directly levered to M&A deal flow, which Goldman forecasts will surge as CEO confidence rebounds and rate visibility improves post-Jackson Hole. Multiple expansion is likely as the street re-rates the business closer to peak-cycle earnings power.
ideas.key_risk: A hawkish surprise from Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole could spike the 10-year yield, suppressing deal activity and pressuring bank valuations.

sources.label: Goldman Sachs Predicts M&A Boom, MS in Focus — Invezz

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley upgraded Ternium to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target lifted to $65 from $55 on August 21.
ideas.thesis: Ternium, the leading flat steel producer in Latin America, trades at a significant discount to global steel peers despite superior EBITDA margins and Mexican nearshoring tailwinds. The $65 MS target implies ~18% upside, supported by automotive and construction demand resilience.
ideas.key_risk: A slowdown in US-Mexico trade flows or renewed tariff escalation could hurt nearshoring-driven steel demand and compress Ternium's margins.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs named Quanta Services a top idea following Q2 2026 earnings, citing accelerating grid modernization and data center power infrastructure backlog.
ideas.thesis: Quanta's multi-year order book in electric transmission and renewable energy interconnection is building at record pace, driven by AI data center power demands and the ongoing energy transition. Revenue visibility extends well into 2027-2028, making the stock relatively defensive in a risk-off environment.
ideas.key_risk: Permitting delays or labor cost inflation could push project timelines and compress margins on fixed-price contracts.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs listed Toast as a top idea post-Q2 2026 earnings, citing accelerating restaurant POS adoption and improving unit economics.
ideas.thesis: Toast is gaining dominant share in the US restaurant technology market with an expanding payments and SaaS ecosystem that creates high switching costs. Gross profit per location is inflecting upward as the company moves up-market into enterprise restaurant chains.
ideas.key_risk: Consumer spending slowdown could reduce restaurant foot traffic and new location additions, weighing on payments volume growth.

ideas.catalyst: Wells Fargo upgraded Portland General Electric to Overweight from Equal Weight, raising the price target to $58 from $51 on August 21.
ideas.thesis: POR is a Pacific Northwest utility with clean energy exposure that stands to benefit from stabilizing long-term interest rates. The $58 Wells Fargo target implies roughly 15% upside, and the stock's dividend yield provides income support while rate expectations shift.
ideas.key_risk: A hawkish Jackson Hole surprise pushing long-term yields sharply higher would pressure utility valuations and erode the dividend premium.

ideas.catalyst: Citigroup upgraded O-I Glass to Buy from Neutral with a $9 target price on August 21, citing compelling valuation at trough conditions.
ideas.thesis: O-I Glass, the world's largest glass packaging manufacturer, trades at distressed multiples despite stabilizing end-market volumes in beer and food segments. The Citi upgrade signals a potential trough in the cycle with scope for significant re-rating as free cash flow recovery becomes visible.
ideas.key_risk: Prolonged weakness in beer volumes (aluminum can substitution) and elevated natural gas costs in European operations could prevent a margin recovery.

deals.headline: Madison Air to Acquire Airflow Technologies for $5.4 Billion
deals.description: Madison Air announced a definitive agreement to acquire Airflow Technologies in an all-cash deal valued at approximately $5.4 billion. The deal represents one of the largest HVAC-adjacent acquisitions of 2026, signaling continued consolidation in the building systems and air management sector.

deals.headline: Alibaba to Sell Videogame Business for At Least $1.5 Billion
deals.description: Alibaba Group confirmed it is selling its videogame division for at least $1.5 billion as part of its ongoing strategic asset rationalization program. The move follows Alibaba's broader portfolio simplification strategy under CEO Eddie Wu, focusing the company on core cloud and commerce businesses.

deals.headline: Ari Emanuel's Mari Acquires Theater Giant ATG Entertainment for $6 Billion
deals.description: Mari, the entertainment company led by Ari Emanuel, announced a $6 billion acquisition of ATG Entertainment, the Broadway and West End theater operator backed by Providence Equity. The deal makes Mari one of the largest live entertainment companies in the world, combining theatrical assets with existing talent and IP management.

deals.headline: Deutsche Telekom Acquires Fiberhost and Inea from Macquarie for ~€1 Billion
deals.description: Deutsche Telekom announced the acquisition of Polish fiber operators Fiberhost and Inea from Macquarie Asset Management for approximately €1 billion. The deal expands Deutsche Telekom's fiber-to-the-home footprint in Central and Eastern Europe, a strategic priority as the company targets 50 million European fiber passings by 2028.

deals.headline: Kaos Capital Launches Activist Campaign at Capricor Therapeutics, Demands Board Overhaul
deals.description: Miami-based Kaos Capital disclosed a significant and growing stake in Capricor Therapeutics and issued a letter demanding an immediate board meeting, nominating two independent directors and pushing for a new committee focused on M&A and strategic alternatives. The action coincides with Capricor's August 22 FDA PDUFA date for deramiocel, which already faces headwinds after an advisory panel voted 9-3 against.
